> Choosing the right tile is a pivotal decision in a master bathroom renovation because the material dictates not only the aesthetic but also the long-term maintenance and durability of the space. > 
> Ceramic tile is often the most budget-friendly choice and is widely available in countless patterns. >

While it is more expensive and harder to cut during installation, its durability often makes it worth the extra effort for long-term performance.
> 
> Natural stone, such as marble, slate, or travertine, offers a unique, organic look that no manufactured tile can replicate. However, stone is porous and requires regular sealing to prevent staining and water damage. It is also softer than porcelain, meaning it can scratch or etch more easily. If you prefer the aesthetic of stone but want lower maintenance, consider porcelain tiles that are printed to look like natural stone.

> Glass tiles are another option, particularly for accent walls or shower surrounds. They reflect light beautifully, making smaller bathrooms feel larger and brighter. > 
> When evaluating these options, consider the slip resistance rating (R-value) for floor tiles, especially if you plan to use the shower as a walk-in. > - Your passport must be valid for **at least 3 months beyond your planned date of departure from the Schengen Area** (Italy).

> #### 3. Avoid Fillers and Unnecessary Additives
> *   Minimize corn, wheat, and soy if possible (though not all dogs are allergic, many do better with limited ingredients).
